reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While both plans prioritize recovery, Plan A incorporates more running volume, specifically 6 easy trail runs, which is crucial for building aerobic base and improving running economy – key factors for speed. Plan B’s focus on rest days and a single strength session feels overly conservative for someone actively trying to increase their speed, and the minimal running volume will likely hinder progress. Plan A’s consistent, albeit easy, running will provide a more effective stimulus for adaptation.
